issues.sym: The brake pedal suddenly sinks toward the floor, the brake warning light comes on, or you find brake fluid dripping along the frame rail. Some owners lost most of their braking with no warning.
issues.why: The steel brake lines run exposed along the frame and corrode from road salt over the years. A rusted line can split under hard braking. Federal regulators investigated this across GM trucks and SUVs of this era, with most failures in snowy, salted states.
issues.next: If the pedal goes soft or fluid is leaking, do not drive the truck. Have every brake line inspected on a lift and replace corroded sections, ideally all of them at once.

issues.t: Clunk felt in the steering wheel
issues.sym: A knock or clunk you can feel through the steering wheel when turning at low speed, parking, or going over bumps.
issues.why: The intermediate steering shaft that links the steering column to the steering gear develops play and binds as its slip joint dries out. GM issued a service bulletin for the noise.
issues.next: Have the steering shaft checked. Lubricating or replacing it usually cures the noise. Get any looseness in the steering looked at promptly.

issues.sym: A Service 4WD message appears on the dash and the truck won't shift into four-wheel drive, takes a long time to engage, or shifts on its own.
issues.why: Usually a fault in the transfer case shift system, such as the shift motor or actuator, its position sensor, or the dash selector switch.
issues.next: Have the 4WD trouble codes read before replacing parts. Check the transfer case fluid level too.

issues.t: Instrument cluster gauges stick or quit
issues.sym: The speedometer, fuel, temperature or oil pressure needle sticks, reads wrong, or drops to zero. Some trucks lose the whole gauge cluster or have dash lights flicker.
issues.why: The small motors that drive each gauge needle fail, and solder joints on the cluster circuit board crack. GM offered special coverage on some 2003-2004 trucks.
issues.next: Have the cluster tested and repaired or rebuilt. Ask a GM dealer whether your truck falls under the old special coverage. Do not rely on a faulty fuel or temperature gauge.

issues.sym: The oil level drops noticeably between changes, with blue smoke at startup, fouled spark plugs, misfires, or a low-oil warning. Most complaints involve 2010-2013 trucks.
issues.why: When the cylinder-deactivation system shuts off cylinders, oil can be drawn past the piston rings. Carbon then sticks the rings and consumption gets worse. GM faced a class action over this engine.
issues.next: Check the oil at every fill-up and never let it run low. Keep records and have a shop run an oil consumption test.

issues.eng: 5.3L and 6.2L V8 with Active Fuel Management
issues.sym: A ticking or tapping from the engine, a misfire code, rough running, and a flashing or steady check engine light. Misfires often show up on the cylinders that shut off for fuel economy.
issues.why: The special lifters used by the cylinder-deactivation system can stick or collapse. A failed lifter can wear the camshaft and send metal through the engine.
issues.next: Have the misfire diagnosed soon. Avoid hard driving and long trips until it is checked, because a failed lifter can damage the camshaft.

issues.sym: Cracks open up in the top of the dash, often near the passenger air bag cover.
issues.why: The dash material breaks down with years of sun and heat.
issues.next: Mostly cosmetic. Use a sunshade and have any crack near the air bag cover looked at.

issues.t: Hard brake pedal from vacuum pump failure (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal suddenly feels hard and the truck takes much longer to stop.
issues.why: These V8s use an engine-driven pump to supply vacuum for the power brakes. Its oil inlet screen can clog and the pump stops making enough vacuum. GM recalled the trucks for a brake module update that uses the anti-lock system to help brake.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. If the pedal turns hard, slow down carefully, leave extra stopping room, and have it repaired before driving normally again.

issues.sym: The air conditioning blows warm, sometimes all at once.
issues.why: The condenser at the front of the truck can crack and leak refrigerant. The hose from the compressor to the condenser can leak too.
issues.next: Have the system leak-tested and fix the leak instead of just recharging it.

issues.t: Lifter failure on V8s with cylinder deactivation
issues.eng: 5.3L and 6.2L V8 with AFM or Dynamic Fuel Management
issues.sym: Ticking from the engine, a chirp at startup, misfire codes, rough running, power loss, or hard starting.
issues.why: The lifters that let the engine shut off cylinders can stick or collapse. A bad lifter can wear the camshaft and spread metal debris through the engine. Owners filed a class action, but GM has not issued a lifter recall.
issues.next: Get a misfire or new tick checked right away and limit driving until it is diagnosed. Repairs usually mean replacing lifters and often the camshaft.

issues.sym: A shudder like driving over rumble strips at steady speeds, harsh 1-2 shifts, jerking near a stop, or a delay when shifting into gear.
issues.why: The original transmission fluid absorbs moisture and lets the torque converter clutch shudder. Shift programming adds to the harshness. GM's bulletin calls for a fluid exchange with a revised fluid.
issues.next: Ask a dealer about GM bulletin 18-NA-355 and any software updates before agreeing to major transmission repairs.

issues.sym: Vibration or clunking from under the truck. If the driveshaft comes apart, the truck loses drive and may be damaged further.
issues.why: A weld on the driveshaft may not have been made correctly at the factory. GM recalled affected trucks.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and get it done. Stop driving and have it towed if you hear a new clunk or feel a strong vibration from underneath.

issues.sym: The rear wheels can suddenly lock while driving, which can make the truck skid.
issues.why: A part in the transmission valve body can cause a sudden downshift that locks the rear wheels. GM recalled affected diesel trucks, then issued a follow-up campaign for some trucks that got the wrong software.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and have it completed before driving the truck normally.

issues.sym: Knocking, rough running, a check engine light, loss of power, or the engine stalling and seizing.
issues.why: Some engines were built with connecting rods or crankshafts out of specification, or with debris in oil passages, which can ruin the bearings. GM recalled affected trucks, and federal investigators are still looking into the problem.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall right away. If the engine knocks or loses power, stop driving and have it towed to a dealer.

issues.sym: A check engine light and possible overheating.
issues.why: The electrically controlled valve that routes coolant can fail. GM extended coverage on the part for 2023 trucks.
issues.next: Watch the temperature gauge and stop if it climbs. Ask a dealer about GM special coverage N252508340.

issues.t: Transfer case can lock the wheels - do not drive (recall)
issues.sym: No warning at all before it happens. The front or rear wheels can suddenly lock up while driving.
issues.why: A part was left out of the transfer case on some four-wheel-drive trucks, which can let the case seize and stop the wheels turning.
issues.next: Do not drive the truck. Have it towed to a dealer, which inspects and replaces the transfer case free under the recall.

issues.t: Rear bumper bracket may be too weak to tow (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing until you tow. The hitch area can flex or give way under trailer load.
issues.why: The bracket behind the rear bumper on some trucks is not strong enough for the rated hitch load, so a trailer can come off.
issues.next: Do not tow until it is checked. The bracket and hitch are replaced free under the recall.

issues.t: Brake warning light may not come on when fluid is low (recall)
issues.sym: No brake warning light even though the brake fluid is low and the pedal may feel soft or travel further than usual.
issues.why: A software fault in the brake control module keeps the low-fluid warning from lighting up, so a leak can go unnoticed.
issues.next: Check the brake fluid level yourself and have the software updated. The update is free and on many trucks can be done over the air.

issues.t: Daytime running lights stay on with the headlights (recall)
issues.sym: The daytime running lights stay lit when the headlights are on, and oncoming drivers flash you about the glare.
issues.why: Body control module software does not switch the running lights off when the headlights come on, which makes the front of the truck too bright at night.
issues.next: Have the body control module software updated. It is free under the recall and often available over the air.
